texts.preamble: Vagat Singh vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:2134) on 10 January, 2024 Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2024:Rj-Jd:2134] High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 505/2004 Vagat Singh son of Jawan Singh, resident of Veravilpur, P.S. Paladi M., Sirohi. (At present lodged in Sirohi Jail) ----Petitioner Versus State of Rajasthan ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr.P.C.Solanki. For Respondent(s) : Mr.Abhishek Purohit, P.P. Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Mathur Order
texts.facts: From the perusal of the record of the case file, it is evident that on 6.5.1996, at around 10.30 am, Food Inspector Laxmichand Jain took samples of curd which was being served by the petitioner with food to the customers at his Dhaba.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the revisionist/petitioner submitted that the sentences so awarded to the revisionist-petitioner were suspended by this Court, vide order dated 3.8.2004 passed in S.B. Criminal Misc. Bail (Suspension of Sentences) Application No.131/2004. Vagat Singh vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:2134) on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130714073/ 1 Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner had undergone detention for some period and the case is pending against him since 1996. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is facing agony of a long protracted trial and therefore, without making any interference on merits/conviction, the sentences awarded to the present revisionist/petitioner may be substituted with the period of sentences already undergone by him. Learned Public Prosecutor opposes the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner. Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in the case of Alister Anthony Pareira Vs. State of Maharashtra (2012)2 SCC 648 and Haripada Das Vs. State of W.B. (1998)9 SCC 678, pleased to observe as under: Alister Anthony Pareira (supra) [2024:RJ-JD:2134] (3 of 3) [CRLR-505/2004] "There is no straitjacket formula for sentencing an accused on proof of crime. The courts have evolved certain principles: twin objective of the sentencing policy is deterrence and correction.
